Do not assign an interpolated string to a String variable first and pass that: the holes are formatted into the text and the protection is gone.

  • Using first As New ShelfContext(options), second As New ShelfContext(options) declares two resources in one Using.

Seeding

Two kinds. HasData in OnModelCreating (used in the model above) seeds rows with fixed keys and is part of the model, so it is included in migrations. UseSeeding (EF Core 9 and later) runs code when the database is created or migrated, which suits data that is computed or that needs the full context. This program ran:

Option Strict On

Imports Microsoft.Data.Sqlite
Imports Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore
Imports Shelf.Core

Module Seeding
    Sub Main()
        Using connection As New SqliteConnection("Data Source=:memory:")
            connection.Open()
            Dim builder As New DbContextOptionsBuilder(Of ShelfContext)()
            builder.UseSqlite(connection)
            builder.UseSeeding(
                Sub(context, storeCreated)
                    Dim set1 = context.Set(Of BookEntity)()
                    If Not set1.Any(Function(b) b.Title = "Dune") Then
                        set1.Add(New BookEntity With {.Title = "Dune", .Year = 1965, .Isbn = Isbn.Parse("9780441172719"), .AuthorId = 1})
                        context.SaveChanges()
                        Console.WriteLine("UseSeeding added Dune (store created by this call: " & storeCreated & ")")
                    End If
                End Sub)

            Using context As New ShelfContext(builder.Options)
                context.Database.EnsureCreated()
                Console.WriteLine("Books: " & context.Books.Count())
            End Using
        End Using
    End Sub
End Module
UseSeeding added Dune (store created by this call: True)
Books: 1

Source: Data seeding

The seeding delegate is a Sub(context, storeCreated) lambda; the second parameter says whether the call created the store. UseAsyncSeeding is the asynchronous counterpart, and both should be written so that running twice does not duplicate rows (the Any check above).

Migrations and Visual Basic

Migrations are where Visual Basic stops working like C#. dotnet ef migrations add generates the migration as source code in the project’s language, and EF Core ships a code generator for C# only. Run against a Visual Basic project, the tool says so:

$ dotnet ef migrations add Initial
Build started...
Build succeeded.
The project language 'VB' isn't supported by the built-in IMigrationsCodeGenerator service. You can try looking for an additional NuGet package which supports this language; moving your DbContext type to a C# class library referenced by this project; or manually implementing and registering the design-time service for the programming language.

(The message is the tool’s own; it names the three ways out.) The options, from simplest to most flexible:

Option Notes

Keep the migrations in a small C# project

The supported route, and the one this page tested. The model (DbContext and entities) stays in Visual Basic; a C# class library holds the generated migrations; the application and the tooling reference both.

EFCore.VisualBasic (community)

A package that adds a Visual Basic code generator to dotnet ef design time. As checked on 2026-10-19, the newest release on NuGet is 8.0.0 (for EF Core 8; earlier ones 7.0.0 and 6.x previews). See the test below: it does not work with EF Core 10.

Hand-written migrations

A migration is a class that derives from Migration with Up and Down methods that call MigrationBuilder; it can be written in Visual Basic, and the ModelSnapshot has to be kept in step by hand, which is the part nobody wants.

EnsureCreated

Creates the schema from the model without migrations. Right for tests and prototypes; it cannot evolve a schema and cannot be mixed with migrations on the same database.

SQL scripts

dotnet ef migrations script produces plain SQL from the C# migrations, to apply with the database’s own tools; or maintain the schema with a dedicated tool outside EF.

The C# migrations project, tested

The layout is three projects: MigData (Visual Basic class library, the model from above), Shelf.Migrations (C# class library that references MigData; migrations go here) and MigApp (the Visual Basic executable that references both, contains the design-time factory and carries the Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design package). The C# project:

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <NuGetAudit>false</NuGetAudit>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <ProjectReference Include="..\MigData\MigData.vbproj" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>

The start-up project registers the migrations assembly and provides the design-time factory (the tool uses it because the executable has no generic host):

Option Strict On

Imports Microsoft.Data.Sqlite
Imports Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore
Imports Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design

Public Class ShelfContextFactory
    Implements IDesignTimeDbContextFactory(Of ShelfContext)

    Public Function CreateDbContext(args As String()) As ShelfContext Implements IDesignTimeDbContextFactory(Of ShelfContext).CreateDbContext
        Return New ShelfContext(CreateOptions("Data Source=shelf.db"))
    End Function

    Public Shared Function CreateOptions(connectionString As String) As DbContextOptions(Of ShelfContext)
        Return New DbContextOptionsBuilder(Of ShelfContext)().
            UseSqlite(connectionString, Sub(o) o.MigrationsAssembly("Shelf.Migrations")).Options
    End Function
End Class

Module Program
    Sub Main()
        Using connection As New SqliteConnection("Data Source=:memory:")
            connection.Open()
            Dim options = New DbContextOptionsBuilder(Of ShelfContext)().
                UseSqlite(connection, Sub(o) o.MigrationsAssembly("Shelf.Migrations")).Options
            Using context As New ShelfContext(options)
                Console.WriteLine("Pending before: " & String.Join(", ", context.Database.GetPendingMigrations().Select(Function(m) m.Substring(m.IndexOf("_"c) + 1))))
                context.Database.Migrate()
                Console.WriteLine("Applied after:  " & String.Join(", ", context.Database.GetAppliedMigrations().Select(Function(m) m.Substring(m.IndexOf("_"c) + 1))))
                Console.WriteLine("Authors seeded: " & context.Authors.Count())
            End Using
        End Using
    End Sub
End Module

The tool is installed once, then the command names the migrations project and the start-up project:

$ dotnet ef migrations add Initial --project MigCs --startup-project MigApp
Build started...
Build succeeded.
Done. To undo this action, use 'ef migrations remove'

$ ls MigCs/Migrations
20261019215308_Initial.Designer.cs
20261019215308_Initial.cs
ShelfContextModelSnapshot.cs

The generated migration is C#, in the C# project, and is not edited by hand (excerpt):

using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Migrations;

#nullable disable

#pragma warning disable CA1814 // Prefer jagged arrays over multidimensional

namespace Shelf.Migrations.Migrations
{
    /// <inheritdoc />
    public partial class Initial : Migration
    {
        /// <inheritdoc />
        protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
        {
            migrationBuilder.CreateTable(
                name: "Authors",
                columns: table => new
                {
                    Id = table.Column<int>(type: "INTEGER", nullable: false)
                        .Annotation("Sqlite:Autoincrement", true),
                    Name = table.Column<string>(type: "TEXT", maxLength: 100, nullable: false)
                },
                constraints: table =>
                {
                    table.PrimaryKey("PK_Authors", x => x.Id);
                });

            migrationBuilder.CreateTable(

Source: Using a separate migrations project, EF Core tools reference (.NET CLI) and Applying migrations

The same documentation lists the other ways to apply migrations (a script, a bundle, Migrate() at start-up); Migrate() at start-up is fine for development and a single instance, while a deployment step is better for anything with more than one instance.

EFCore.VisualBasic, tested

EFCore.VisualBasic is a community project, published by an EF team member on the project’s own repository, that registers a Visual Basic migrations generator through IDesignTimeServices. The test installed EntityFrameworkCore.VisualBasic 8.0.0 next to EF Core 10.0.13. Restore warns first:

warning NU1608: Detected package version outside of dependency constraint: EntityFrameworkCore.VisualBasic 8.0.0 requires Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design (>= 8.0.2 && < 9.0.0) but version Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design 10.0.13 was resolved.
warning NU1608: Detected package version outside of dependency constraint: Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.VisualBasic 4.5.0 requires Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Common (= 4.5.0) but version Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Common 5.0.0 was resolved.

With warnings as errors off, the project builds and the services class (EFCoreVisualBasicServices.ConfigureDesignTimeServices) compiles, but running the tool fails inside Roslyn:

$ dotnet ef migrations add Initial --no-build
Method 'GetForEachSymbols' in type 'Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.VisualBasic.Utilities.SpeculationAnalyzer' from assembly 'Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.VisualBasic.Workspaces, Version=4.5.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35' does not have an implementation.
Could not load type 'Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.LanguageService.AbstractBlockFacts' from assembly 'Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces, Version=5.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35'.

So with EF Core 10 the C# migrations project is the working route. If the project publishes a version for the EF Core release you use, the package would remove the need for the second project; re-check its NuGet page before relying on either statement.

Source: Reverse engineering (scaffolding) describes the plug-in model that community code generators use, and the package page (community) lists its versions.

Reverse engineering (dotnet ef dbcontext scaffold) has the same limit: it writes C# entity classes. Scaffold into a C# project and reference it, or write the entities by hand.

Binding query results to Windows Forms and WPF

For a grid in Windows Forms the shape is: load into a list, wrap it in a BindingList(Of T) or a BindingSource, set DataGridView.DataSource. EF Core can also provide a ready local view (context.Books.Local.ToBindingList()), which stays in step with the change tracker. The listing below was built, not run (Windows Forms needs Windows); the Async Sub override is the correct place to start asynchronous loading because it runs on the UI thread and resumes there.

Option Strict On

Imports System.ComponentModel
Imports System.Windows.Forms
Imports Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore

Public Class BookRow
    Public Property Id As Integer
    Public Property Title As String = ""
    Public Property Year As Integer
End Class

Public Class RowsContext
    Inherits DbContext

    Public Property Books As DbSet(Of BookRow)

    Protected Overrides Sub OnConfiguring(optionsBuilder As DbContextOptionsBuilder)
        optionsBuilder.UseSqlite("Data Source=shelf.db")
    End Sub
End Class

Public Class BookGridForm
    Inherits Form

    Private ReadOnly _grid As New DataGridView() With {.Dock = DockStyle.Fill, .AutoGenerateColumns = True}
    Private ReadOnly _source As New BindingSource()
    Private ReadOnly _rows As New BindingList(Of BookRow)

    Public Sub New()
        Text = "Shelf"
        _source.DataSource = _rows
        _grid.DataSource = _source
        Controls.Add(_grid)
    End Sub

    Public Shared Function TrackedRows(context As RowsContext) As BindingList(Of BookRow)
        ' A binding list that stays in step with the change tracker.
        Return context.Books.Local.ToBindingList()
    End Function

    Protected Overrides Async Sub OnShown(e As EventArgs)
        MyBase.OnShown(e)
        Using context As New RowsContext()
            ' AsNoTracking: the grid edits copies; save them explicitly with a separate unit of work.
            Dim loaded = Await context.Books.AsNoTracking().OrderBy(Function(b) b.Title).ToListAsync()
            _rows.RaiseListChangedEvents = False
            For Each row In loaded
                _rows.Add(row)
            Next
            _rows.RaiseListChangedEvents = True
            _rows.ResetBindings()
        End Using
    End Sub
End Class

Public Module Program
    <STAThread>
    Public Sub Main()
        Application.EnableVisualStyles()
        Application.Run(New BookGridForm())
    End Sub
End Module

Source: Windows Forms for .NET

Notes: the entity here is a row class for the grid, with settable properties (a grid cannot edit read-only ones); the context loads with AsNoTracking because the grid edits copies and the program saves them explicitly; RaiseListChangedEvents = False while adding many rows avoids one grid refresh per row; do not keep the context alive for the lifetime of the form. For WPF the equivalent is an ObservableCollection(Of BookViewModel) that the view model fills after Await returns (see WPF Applications), and a DataTable.DefaultView binds to a DataGrid in both frameworks. The Windows Forms details (BindingSource, DataGridView columns) are on Windows Forms Applications.

Other stores: MongoDB and Redis

Document and key-value stores have their own drivers, which are .NET libraries and therefore work from Visual Basic. The listing was built, not run: it needs servers on localhost. It uses MongoDB.Driver 3.12.0 and StackExchange.Redis 3.4.5 with expression lambdas in the queries (the Mongo Find takes an expression tree, as LINQ does):

Option Strict On

Imports MongoDB.Bson
Imports MongoDB.Driver
Imports StackExchange.Redis

' Built, not run: both stores need a running server.
Public Class BookDocument
    Public Property Id As ObjectId
    Public Property Title As String = ""
    Public Property Year As Integer
End Class

Module Program
    Sub Main()
        RunAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult()
    End Sub

    Private Async Function RunAsync() As Task
        Dim client As New MongoClient("mongodb://localhost:27017")
        Dim books = client.GetDatabase("shelf").GetCollection(Of BookDocument)("books")
        Await books.InsertOneAsync(New BookDocument With {.Title = "Dune", .Year = 1965})
        Dim newer = Await books.Find(Function(b) b.Year > 1960).SortBy(Function(b) b.Title).ToListAsync()
        Console.WriteLine("Mongo documents: " & newer.Count)

        Dim redis = Await ConnectionMultiplexer.ConnectAsync("localhost:6379")
        Dim db = redis.GetDatabase()
        Await db.StringSetAsync("book:1:title", "Dune", TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5))
        Dim cached As RedisValue = Await db.StringGetAsync("book:1:title")
        Console.WriteLine("Redis value: " & cached.ToString())
    End Function
End Module

The data models, indexing and operations of these stores are explained with their native tools in MongoDB drivers and tooling and Redis clients and client-side caching; Choosing the right database helps to decide which store a feature needs.

Legacy: EF6, LINQ to SQL and typed DataSets

  • EF6 (EntityFramework 6.x, the System.Data.Entity namespace) is in maintenance. The 6.5 line targets .NET and .NET Framework: a project test on .NET 10 restored EntityFramework 6.5.1, compiled a DbContext-derived class, and loaded the assembly at run time (EF6 type loaded: EntityFramework 6.0.0.0, Runtime: .NET 10.0.13). The test did not open a database; the EDMX designer and the Package Manager Console commands of EF6 (Enable-Migrations, Update-Database) were not exercised. For an application that already uses EF6, keeping it on .NET Framework is legitimate; moving to .NET 10 is a port to EF Core in practice, covered for C# on Data Access with EF6. The official guide for the move is Port from EF6 to EF Core.

  • LINQ to SQL (System.Data.Linq, .dbml designer files) is documented in the .NET Framework data documentation (the link below sits under /dotnet/framework/), not in the .NET documentation. Plan to port a program that uses it to EF Core or Dapper as part of a move to .NET 10.

  • Typed DataSets generated by older Visual Studio wizards are plain code on top of System.Data and port easily, but they are not a model to start from.

  • System.Data.OracleClient and System.Data.SqlClient are the old provider names; see the opening table.

Source: Entity Framework 6, Compare EF Core and EF6 and LINQ to SQL (.NET Framework)

SqliteException (error 19)

CHECK constraint failed: Balance >= 0

Query EF Core cannot translate

InvalidOperationException

The LINQ expression ... could not be translated.

Two contexts update the same row

DbUpdateConcurrencyException

Raised by SaveChanges of the second context.

SQL Server unreachable

SqlException (Number 0)

A network-related or instance-specific error occurred while establishing a connection to SQL Server.

Cancelled token

TaskCanceledException

Derives from OperationCanceledException.

Pitfalls

Pitfall Remedy

Nothing as a parameter value

DBNull.Value.

String-concatenated SQL

Parameters; allow-list identifiers.

AddWithValue with strings against SQL Server

Add(name, SqlDbType.NVarChar, size).Value.

Await in Catch or Finally

Capture, leave the block, then await (BC36943).

Visual Basic Like in a LINQ query

EF.Functions.Like.

Option Compare Text in a file with EF queries

Option Compare Binary; collation in the database.

String properties are nullable in EF Core

IsRequired().

Local variable named like a type or a DbSet

Rename; names are case-insensitive.

Trying dotnet ef migrations add in a VB project

Use a C# migrations project.

One shared DbContext for the whole application

One per unit of work.

Leaked connection

Using everywhere; do not store connections in fields.

TrustServerCertificate=True to silence a certificate error

Fix the certificate; use the flag only for throw-away local servers.

Connection string in source control

Configuration, user secrets, a key vault or integrated security.

Unbounded query bound to a grid

Page in the query (Skip/Take); see pagination strategies.
